Operational Summary

Across all 328,521 departed flights originating from New York City (JFK, LGA, EWR) in 2013, the majority left within standard operating windows:

On-Time / Early
60.9%
200,089 flights (≤ 0 min)
Minor Delay
17.6%
57,658 flights (1–15 min)
FAA Delayed
21.5%
70,774 flights (> 15 min)
Severe Delay
8.1%
26,581 flights (> 60 min)
  • 60.9% departed early or on the exact scheduled minute.
  • 17.6% experienced minor adjustments under 15 minutes, which commercial airlines classify as on-time under FAA standard A14 metrics.
  • 21.5% incurred official delays exceeding 15 minutes.
  • 8.1% suffered acute disruptions exceeding 60 minutes.

Official Delay Attribution (BTS Benchmark)

Official records from the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) and Federal Aviation Administration identify five core drivers of schedule delays:

1. Late-Arriving Aircraft (Network Propagation) ~38%
Planes fly multiple route segments each day. Upstream inbound delays automatically cascade downstream to subsequent flights.
2. Air Carrier Operations ~30%
Operational factors under carrier oversight: unscheduled maintenance, crew legal duty hour caps, ramp baggage handling, and cabin turnaround.
3. NAS & Airspace Congestion ~24%
Air traffic control route spacing, high terminal-area density, ground delay programs (GDP), and airport surface taxiway queues.
4. Severe Weather Disruptions ~7%
Meteorological events requiring airspace corridor rerouting or safety ground stops (thunderstorms, snowstorms, visibility minima).
5. Security Breaches <1%
Infrequent terminal concourse re-screenings or security perimeter hold procedures.
